newsitem.title: TURKEY: ISTANBUL EXCHANGE LISTS TEXTILE FIRM BOYASAN.
newsitem.headline: ISTANBUL EXCHANGE LISTS TEXTILE FIRM BOYASAN.

text.p: Istanbul Stock Exchange listed publicly owned shares of textile firm Boyasan Tekstil Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. on the national market at an opening price of 11,000 lira per 1,000 lira nominal share on Thursday.
The company had last week sold 87.5 billion lira of new and old shares, or 35 percent of its capital to public when raising its capital to 250 billion lira from previous 200 billion.

Inter Yatirim securities, leader of the consortium which managed the public offer, said 55.54 billion lira of the offer was sold to 11,100 domestic investors, 27.11 billion lira to nine foreign financial institutions and 4.85 billion lira to domestic institutional investors.
It said Donaldson Lufkin Jenrette Int.Ltd. and Republic National Bank of New York each bought 6.25 billion lira worth shares from the offer.

Boyasan, which is part of Turkey's leading textile exporting group Uslu Holding is active in dyeing and stamping of fabrics. After the public offer, its 58.6 percent stake is owned by Tumteks Tekstil, compared to previous 92 percent.
The company had earlier said it would use income from the public offer to pay down its financial debts.
Its 1996 net profits were 167.6 billion lira and net sales were 2.75 trillion lira, up sharply from 20.4 billion and 1.31 trillion lira, respectively a year ago.
Boyasan shares traded lower at 9,500 lira in the afternoon session and Tumteks shares at 8,400 lira, down from Wednesday's 9,000. The market index fell sharply in the afternoon.
